customer_question: If we register our product as Core-Complete referencing a Qualcomm DN (without a separate Core-Controller DN), and Qualcomm later updates their Core-Complete DN, would we need to redo the RF/RF PHY tests? Would creating a Core-Controller DN now protect us from future re-testing?
question_variants: Does creating a Core-Controller DN protect against future RF re-testing when the Host/Core-Complete DN updates?
What happens to our RF certification if the Qualcomm DN we referenced gets updated?
Is it worth getting a separate Core-Controller DN to future-proof the RF registration?
actual_issue: A customer ([COMPANY] Alps Alpine) planning to register a Volvo automotive unit as a Core-Complete (formerly End Product) registration asked: if they use Qualcomm's RF-less Core-Complete DN + product-level RF test evidence, and Qualcomm later updates their Core-Complete DN, would the RF tests need to be redone? The consultant confirmed: yes, if the Qualcomm Core-Complete DN is updated, the product would need to re-register referencing the new DN - and without a product-owned Core-Controller DN, the RF evidence (test reports) would need to be re-run and re-uploaded. However, if the customer now creates their own Core-Controller DN (which includes the product's RF evidence), then in future re-registrations they can include their own Core-Controller DN regardless of Qualcomm's updates, avoiding RF re-testing. The cost for this approach: 2x SIG Qualification Fee (one for Core-Controller DN, one for Core-Complete DN), but the same service fee applies as for a single registration.
plain_english_explanation: In Bluetooth SIG certification, a product can be registered either as a Core-Complete (the full product registration) or split into a Core-Controller (covering the radio/controller layer, including RF evidence) plus a Core-Complete (covering the host/profile layer) that references the Core-Controller. If a customer registers only as Core-Complete and references a chip vendor's (Qualcomm's) Host+X2Core DN without owning a Core-Controller DN, then when the chip vendor updates their DN, the customer must re-register their Core-Complete referencing the new DN - and since there is no owned Core-Controller DN, the RF test evidence is re-evaluated and potentially needs to be re-run. By creating their own Core-Controller DN first (using the product's RF test evidence), the customer owns that DN. Future updates to Qualcomm's Host DN can then be handled by creating a new Core-Complete that includes the customer's existing Core-Controller DN, skipping RF re-testing entirely. The trade-off: 2x SIG Qualification Fee, but the same service cost.

Yes, obtaining a Core-Controller DN requires one additional registration fee, but future Qualcomm DN updates can be handled by including your own DN, avoiding re-testing.)
decision_logic: When a product uses a SoC-based design with a chip vendor Host DN and is considering a Core-Complete-only registration: (1) Assess whether the chip vendor is likely to update their Host/Core-Complete DN in the near future (e.g., annual Android updates from Qualcomm). (2) If yes, recommend creating a product-owned Core-Controller DN now at the cost of an additional SIG Qualification Fee, protecting against future RF re-testing. (3) Quote two options: (a) Core-Complete only (lower immediate cost, RF re-test risk in future) and (b) Core-Controller + Core-Complete (higher immediate cost, future-proof against RF re-test). (4) Service fee is the same for both options; only the SIG Qualification Fee differs.
final_recommendation: For products in ecosystems where chip vendor DNs update frequently (e.g., Qualcomm Android updates), proactively offer the Core-Controller + Core-Complete registration path as a future-proofing option. Clearly communicate the trade-off: 2x SIG Qualification Fee now vs. potential RF re-testing cost in the future. For automotive products with long product lifecycles and frequent platform software updates, the Core-Controller DN approach is often the more cost-effective long-term strategy.
risk_if_done_wrong: Registering as Core-Complete-only when the chip vendor's DN updates regularly means repeated RF re-testing with each major update - potentially costly over a product's multi-year lifetime. Conversely, paying for Core-Controller DN when the chip vendor's DN is stable wastes the additional Qualification Fee.
